# dsysvx

> Computes the solution to system of linear equations A·X = B for symmetric matrices.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import dsysvx from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/dsysvx';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
dsysvx(
    order,
    fact, uplo,
    N, nrhs,
    A, LDA,
    AF, LDAF,
    IPIV, strideIPIV,
    B, LDB,
    X, LDX,
    rcond,
    FERR, strideFERR,
    BERR, strideBERR,
    WORK,
    IWORK
) → integer
```

| param | type | intent | shape | constraints | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `order` | `Layout` | in |  | one of `'row-major'`, `'column-major'` | storage layout ('row-major' or 'column-major') |
| `fact` | `("not-factored"\|"factored")` | in |  | one of `'factored'`, `'not-factored'` | specifies whether or not the factored form of A has been supplied on entry. `'factored'`: On entry, AF and IPIV contain the factored form of A. AF and IPIV will not be modified. `'not-factored'`: The matrix A will be copied to AF and factored. |
| `uplo` | `MatrixTriangle` | in |  | one of `'lower'`, `'upper'` | `'upper'`: Upper triangle of A is stored; `'lower'`: Lower triangle of A is stored. |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  | requires `N ≥ 0` | the number of linear equations, i.e., the order of the matrix A. |
| `nrhs` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  | requires `nrhs ≥ 0` | the number of right hand sides, i.e., the number of columns of the matrices B and X. |
| `A` | `Float64Array` | in | `N × N` |  | the symmetric matrix A. |
| ↳ `LDA` | `PositiveInteger` | in |  | requires `LDA ≥ max( 1, N )` | leading dimension of `A` |
| `AF` | `Float64Array` | in/out | `N × N` |  | if `fact === 'factored'`, then AF is an input argument and on entry contains the block diagonal matrix D and the multipliers used to obtain the factor U or L from the factorization A = U*D*U**T or A = L*D*L**T as computed by DSYTRF. |
| ↳ `LDAF` | `PositiveInteger` | in |  | requires `LDAF ≥ max( 1, N )` | leading dimension of `AF` |
| `IPIV` | `Int32Array` | in/out | `N` |  | if `fact === 'factored'`, then IPIV is an input argument and on entry contains details of the interchanges and the block structure of D, as determined by DSYTRF (0-based). |
| ↳ `strideIPIV` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride length for `IPIV` |
| `B` | `Float64Array` | in | `N × nrhs` |  | the N-by-NRHS right hand side matrix B. |
| ↳ `LDB` | `PositiveInteger` | in |  | column-major requires `LDB ≥ max( 1, N )`; row-major requires `LDB ≥ max( 1, nrhs )` | leading dimension of `B` |
| `X` | `Float64Array` | out | `N × nrhs` |  | if INFO = 0 or INFO = N+1, the N-by-NRHS solution matrix X. |
| ↳ `LDX` | `PositiveInteger` | in |  | column-major requires `LDX ≥ max( 1, N )`; row-major requires `LDX ≥ max( 1, nrhs )` | leading dimension of `X` |
| `rcond` | `Float64Array` | out |  |  | the estimate of the reciprocal condition number of the matrix A. |
| `FERR` | `Float64Array` | out | `nrhs` |  | the estimated forward error bound for each solution vector X(j) (the j-th column of the solution matrix X). |
| ↳ `strideFERR` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride length for `FERR` |
| `BERR` | `Float64Array` | out | `nrhs` |  | the componentwise relative backward error of each solution vector X(j) (i.e., the smallest relative change in any element of A or B that makes X(j) an exact solution). |
| ↳ `strideBERR` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride length for `BERR` |
| `WORK` | `(Float64Array\|null)` | out | `≥ max( 1, 3 * N )` |  | caller-provided workspace of at least `max( 1, 3 * N )` elements; for optimum performance, when `fact` is `'not-factored'`, `max( 1, 3 * N, N * NB )` (`NB = 64`, the dsytrf block size from `ilaenv`); or `null` to allocate the optimal size |
| `IWORK` | `(Int32Array\|null)` | out | `≥ N` |  | caller-provided workspace of at least `N` elements |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `fact`: Specifies whether or not the factored form of A has been supplied on entry.

  -   `= 'F'`: On entry, `AF` and `IPIV` contain the factored form of A.  `AF` and `IPIV` will not be modified.
  -   `= 'N'`: The matrix A will be copied to `AF` and factored.
- `uplo`:

  -   `= 'U'`: Upper triangle of A is stored;
  -   `= 'L'`: Lower triangle of A is stored.
- `N`: The number of linear equations, i.e., the order of the matrix A. $N \ge 0$.
- `nrhs`: The number of right hand sides, i.e., the number of columns of the matrices B and X. $\mathrm{NRHS} \ge 0$.
- `A`: The symmetric matrix A. If `UPLO = 'U'`, the leading N-by-N upper triangular part of A contains the upper triangular part of the matrix A, and the strictly lower triangular part of A is not referenced. If `UPLO = 'L'`, the leading N-by-N lower triangular part of A contains the lower triangular part of the matrix A, and the strictly upper triangular part of A is not referenced.
- `AF`: If `FACT = 'F'`, then `AF` is an input argument and on entry contains the block diagonal matrix D and the multipliers used to obtain the factor U or L from the factorization $A = U \, D \, U^T$ or $A = L \, D \, L^T$ as computed by DSYTRF.

  If `FACT = 'N'`, then `AF` is an output argument and on exit returns the block diagonal matrix D and the multipliers used to obtain the factor U or L from the factorization $A = U \, D \, U^T$ or $A = L \, D \, L^T$.
- `IPIV`: If `FACT = 'F'`, then `IPIV` is an input argument and on entry contains details of the interchanges and the block structure of D, as determined by DSYTRF. If $\mathrm{IPIV}(k) > 0$, then rows and columns k and `IPIV(k)` were interchanged and D(k,k) is a 1-by-1 diagonal block. If `UPLO = 'U'` and $\mathrm{IPIV}(k) = \mathrm{IPIV}(k-1) < 0$, then rows and columns k-1 and -`IPIV(k)` were interchanged and D(k-1:k,k-1:k) is a 2-by-2 diagonal block. If `UPLO = 'L'` and $\mathrm{IPIV}(k) = \mathrm{IPIV}(k+1) < 0$, then rows and columns k+1 and -`IPIV(k)` were interchanged and D(k:k+1,k:k+1) is a 2-by-2 diagonal block.

  If `FACT = 'N'`, then `IPIV` is an output argument and on exit contains details of the interchanges and the block structure of D, as determined by DSYTRF.
- `B`: The N-by-`NRHS` right hand side matrix B.
- `X`: If `INFO = 0` or $\mathrm{INFO} = N+1$, the N-by-`NRHS` solution matrix X.
- `rcond`: The estimate of the reciprocal condition number of the matrix A. If `RCOND` is less than the machine precision (in particular, if `RCOND = 0`), the matrix is singular to working precision. This condition is indicated by a return code of $\mathrm{INFO} > 0$.
- `FERR`: The estimated forward error bound for each solution vector `X(j)` (the j-th column of the solution matrix X). If XTRUE is the true solution corresponding to `X(j)`, `FERR(j)` is an estimated upper bound for the magnitude of the largest element in (`X(j)` - XTRUE) divided by the magnitude of the largest element in `X(j)`. The estimate is as reliable as the estimate for `RCOND`, and is almost always a slight overestimate of the true error.
- `BERR`: The componentwise relative backward error of each solution vector `X(j)` (i.e., the smallest relative change in any element of A or B that makes `X(j)` an exact solution).
- `WORK`: On exit, if `INFO = 0`, `WORK(1)` returns the optimal `LWORK`.

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: info status code

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid order
- `TypeError` second argument must be one of the following: "factored", "not-factored"
- `TypeError` third argument must be a valid matrix triangle
- `RangeError` fourth argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` fifth argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` seventh argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, N )`
- `RangeError` ninth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, N )`
- `RangeError` thirteenth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, N )` (column-major)
- `RangeError` thirteenth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, nrhs )` (row-major)
- `RangeError` fifteenth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, N )` (column-major)
- `RangeError` fifteenth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, nrhs )` (row-major)
- `TypeError` if a string argument is not a valid option

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
dsysvx.ndarray(
    fact, uplo,
    N, nrhs,
    A, strideA1, strideA2, offsetA,
    AF, strideAF1, strideAF2, offsetAF,
    IPIV, strideIPIV, offsetIPIV,
    B, strideB1, strideB2, offsetB,
    X, strideX1, strideX2, offsetX,
    rcond,
    FERR, strideFERR, offsetFERR,
    BERR, strideBERR, offsetBERR,
    WORK, strideWork, offsetWork,
    IWORK, strideIWork, offsetIWork
) → info: integer
```

Solves a real symmetric indefinite system of linear equations A_X = B using.
_ the diagonal pivoting factorization A = U_D_U^T or A = L_D*L^T, and provides
an estimate of the condition number and error bounds on the solution.

Matrix shapes are logical (rows × columns). The reference's leading dimension (`LDA`, …) is replaced by the two strides and the offset.

| param | type | intent | shape | constraints | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `fact` | `("not-factored"\|"factored")` | in |  | one of `'factored'`, `'not-factored'` | 'factored' if AF and IPIV contain the factorization, 'not-factored' to compute it |
| `uplo` | `MatrixTriangle` | in |  | one of `'lower'`, `'upper'` | 'upper' if upper triangle of A stored, 'lower' if lower triangle |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  | requires `N ≥ 0` | order of the matrix A |
| `nrhs` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  | requires `nrhs ≥ 0` | number of right-hand side columns |
| `A` | `Float64Array` | in | `N × N` |  | symmetric matrix A (column-major, only triangle specified by uplo stored) |
| ↳ `strideA1` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the first dimension of A |
| ↳ `strideA2` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the second dimension of A |
| ↳ `offsetA` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for A |
| `AF` | `Float64Array` | in/out | `N × N` |  | factored form of A (output if FACT='not-factored', input if FACT='factored') |
| ↳ `strideAF1` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the first dimension of AF |
| ↳ `strideAF2` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the second dimension of AF |
| ↳ `offsetAF` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for AF |
| `IPIV` | `Int32Array` | in/out | `N` |  | pivot indices (output if FACT='not-factored', input if FACT='factored') |
| ↳ `strideIPIV` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for IPIV |
| ↳ `offsetIPIV` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for IPIV |
| `B` | `Float64Array` | in | `N × nrhs` |  | right-hand side matrix (column-major, N-by-NRHS) |
| ↳ `strideB1` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the first dimension of B |
| ↳ `strideB2` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the second dimension of B |
| ↳ `offsetB` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for B |
| `X` | `Float64Array` | out | `N × nrhs` |  | solution matrix (column-major, N-by-NRHS, output) |
| ↳ `strideX1` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the first dimension of X |
| ↳ `strideX2` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the second dimension of X |
| ↳ `offsetX` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for X |
| `rcond` | `Float64Array` | out |  |  | single-element array for reciprocal condition number (output) |
| `FERR` | `Float64Array` | out | `nrhs` |  | forward error bounds array (length NRHS, output) |
| ↳ `strideFERR` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for FERR |
| ↳ `offsetFERR` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for FERR |
| `BERR` | `Float64Array` | out | `nrhs` |  | backward error bounds array (length NRHS, output) |
| ↳ `strideBERR` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for BERR |
| ↳ `offsetBERR` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for BERR |
| `WORK` | `Float64Array` | out | `≥ max( 1, 3 * N )` |  | workspace array (length at least max(1, 3*N)) |
| ↳ `strideWork` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for WORK |
| ↳ `offsetWork` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for WORK |
| `IWORK` | `Int32Array` | out | `≥ N` |  | integer workspace array (length at least N) |
| ↳ `strideIWork` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for IWORK |
| ↳ `offsetIWork` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for IWORK |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `fact`: Specifies whether or not the factored form of A has been supplied on entry.

  -   `= 'F'`: On entry, `AF` and `IPIV` contain the factored form of A.  `AF` and `IPIV` will not be modified.
  -   `= 'N'`: The matrix A will be copied to `AF` and factored.
- `uplo`:

  -   `= 'U'`: Upper triangle of A is stored;
  -   `= 'L'`: Lower triangle of A is stored.
- `N`: The number of linear equations, i.e., the order of the matrix A. $N \ge 0$.
- `nrhs`: The number of right hand sides, i.e., the number of columns of the matrices B and X. $\mathrm{NRHS} \ge 0$.
- `A`: The symmetric matrix A. If `UPLO = 'U'`, the leading N-by-N upper triangular part of A contains the upper triangular part of the matrix A, and the strictly lower triangular part of A is not referenced. If `UPLO = 'L'`, the leading N-by-N lower triangular part of A contains the lower triangular part of the matrix A, and the strictly upper triangular part of A is not referenced.
- `AF`: If `FACT = 'F'`, then `AF` is an input argument and on entry contains the block diagonal matrix D and the multipliers used to obtain the factor U or L from the factorization $A = U \, D \, U^T$ or $A = L \, D \, L^T$ as computed by DSYTRF.

  If `FACT = 'N'`, then `AF` is an output argument and on exit returns the block diagonal matrix D and the multipliers used to obtain the factor U or L from the factorization $A = U \, D \, U^T$ or $A = L \, D \, L^T$.
- `IPIV`: If `FACT = 'F'`, then `IPIV` is an input argument and on entry contains details of the interchanges and the block structure of D, as determined by DSYTRF. If $\mathrm{IPIV}(k) > 0$, then rows and columns k and `IPIV(k)` were interchanged and D(k,k) is a 1-by-1 diagonal block. If `UPLO = 'U'` and $\mathrm{IPIV}(k) = \mathrm{IPIV}(k-1) < 0$, then rows and columns k-1 and -`IPIV(k)` were interchanged and D(k-1:k,k-1:k) is a 2-by-2 diagonal block. If `UPLO = 'L'` and $\mathrm{IPIV}(k) = \mathrm{IPIV}(k+1) < 0$, then rows and columns k+1 and -`IPIV(k)` were interchanged and D(k:k+1,k:k+1) is a 2-by-2 diagonal block.

  If `FACT = 'N'`, then `IPIV` is an output argument and on exit contains details of the interchanges and the block structure of D, as determined by DSYTRF.
- `B`: The N-by-`NRHS` right hand side matrix B.
- `X`: If `INFO = 0` or $\mathrm{INFO} = N+1$, the N-by-`NRHS` solution matrix X.
- `rcond`: The estimate of the reciprocal condition number of the matrix A. If `RCOND` is less than the machine precision (in particular, if `RCOND = 0`), the matrix is singular to working precision. This condition is indicated by a return code of $\mathrm{INFO} > 0$.
- `FERR`: The estimated forward error bound for each solution vector `X(j)` (the j-th column of the solution matrix X). If XTRUE is the true solution corresponding to `X(j)`, `FERR(j)` is an estimated upper bound for the magnitude of the largest element in (`X(j)` - XTRUE) divided by the magnitude of the largest element in `X(j)`. The estimate is as reliable as the estimate for `RCOND`, and is almost always a slight overestimate of the true error.
- `BERR`: The componentwise relative backward error of each solution vector `X(j)` (i.e., the smallest relative change in any element of A or B that makes `X(j)` an exact solution).
- `WORK`: On exit, if `INFO = 0`, `WORK(1)` returns the optimal `LWORK`.

</details>

**Returns** `info: integer`: 0 if successful, k>0 if D(k,k) is zero (singular), N+1 if rcond < machine epsilon

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be one of the following: "factored", "not-factored"
- `TypeError` second argument must be a valid matrix triangle
- `RangeError` third argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` fourth argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` `IWORK` must have at least `N` elements from `offsetIWork`

### Status codes

An `info` status code: `0` on success. A positive value reports a numerical condition such as a singular pivot or a failure to converge (see the description). Invalid arguments throw instead of returning a negative `info`.

The reference documents `INFO` as:

-   `= 0`: successful exit
-   `< 0`: if `INFO = -i`, the i-th argument had an illegal value
-   `> 0`: if `INFO = i`, and i is \<= N:  D(i,i) is exactly zero.  The factorization has been completed but the factor D is exactly singular, so the solution and error bounds could not be computed. `RCOND = 0` is returned. = N+1: D is nonsingular, but `RCOND` is less than machine precision, meaning that the matrix is singular to working precision.  Nevertheless, the solution and error bounds are computed because there are a number of situations where the computed solution can be more accurate than the value of `RCOND` would suggest.

## Notes

-   `dsysvx()` corresponds to the reference LAPACK routine [`DSYSVX`](https://github.com/Reference-LAPACK/lapack/blob/v3.12.0/SRC/dsysvx.f).

</section>

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import Float64Array from '@stdlib/array/float64/lib/index.js';
import Int32Array from '@stdlib/array/int32/lib/index.js';
import dsysvx from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/dsysvx';

const N = 3;
const nrhs = 1;

// Symmetric matrix A (column-major); B = A * [ 1, 1, 1 ]^T:
let A = new Float64Array( [ 4.0, 1.0, 2.0, 1.0, 5.0, 3.0, 2.0, 3.0, 6.0 ] );
let B = new Float64Array( [ 7.0, 9.0, 11.0 ] );
let AF = new Float64Array( N * N );
let X = new Float64Array( N * nrhs );
let IPIV = new Int32Array( N );
let rcond = new Float64Array( 1 );
let FERR = new Float64Array( nrhs );
let BERR = new Float64Array( nrhs );
let WORK = new Float64Array( 3 * N );
let IWORK = new Int32Array( N );

// Using the standard interface:
let info = dsysvx( 'column-major', 'not-factored', 'upper', N, nrhs, A, N, AF, N, IPIV, 1, B, N, X, N, rcond, FERR, 1, BERR, 1, WORK, IWORK );
console.log( info ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
console.log( X ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
console.log( rcond[ 0 ] ); // eslint-disable-line no-console

// Using the ndarray interface:
A = new Float64Array( [ 4.0, 1.0, 2.0, 1.0, 5.0, 3.0, 2.0, 3.0, 6.0 ] );
B = new Float64Array( [ 7.0, 9.0, 11.0 ] );
AF = new Float64Array( N * N );
X = new Float64Array( N * nrhs );
IPIV = new Int32Array( N );
rcond = new Float64Array( 1 );
FERR = new Float64Array( nrhs );
BERR = new Float64Array( nrhs );
WORK = new Float64Array( 3 * N );
IWORK = new Int32Array( N );
info = dsysvx.ndarray( 'not-factored', 'upper', N, nrhs, A, 1, N, 0, AF, 1, N, 0, IPIV, 1, 0, B, 1, N, 0, X, 1, N, 0, rcond, FERR, 1, 0, BERR, 1, 0, WORK, 1, 0, IWORK, 1, 0 );
console.log( info ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
console.log( X ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
```

</section>

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `DSYSVX`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

DSYSVX uses the diagonal pivoting factorization to compute the solution to a real system of linear equations $A \, X = B$, where A is an N-by-N symmetric matrix and X and B are N-by-`NRHS` matrices.

Error bounds on the solution and a condition estimate are also provided.

</section>
